title: Dark web threat actor de-anonymization
description:
• Background The dark web has become a preferred operating space for threat actors in the modern age, mainly because it lets them hide their identity behind Tor hidden services, which makes attribution of threat actors operating on darkweb the main challenge for any investigation. Such threat actors carry out a wide range of unlawful activities such as drugs and arms sale, stolen data and hacking services, money laundering, terror financing, etc. The objective of this problem statement is to build a system for the deanonymization of dark web threat actors and link them to suspect real-world entities.
• Description The system shall deanonymize dark web threat actors by continuously gathering their footprints from a range of sources (marketplaces, forums, deep web etc.) and linking them to the identifying information available on those sources. The system envisages three core capabilities. First, finding misconfigurations in Tor hidden services-such as exposed server-status pages, SSL certificates tied to clearnet domains, default service banners, descriptor inconsistencies, etc and matching them with clearnet infrastructure to point to the likely origin servers. Second, mapping threat actors across multiple marketplaces into a single relationship graph of handles, PGP keys, wallets and trust links. Third, using AI-based analysis, including stylometric persona identification and behavioural profiling, to link rebranded or migrated personas to known threat actors. The system shall provide an analytical front end to query the database across a chosen timeline and shall work in an autonomous mode, drawing on available sources of good quality and reliability.
• Expected Solution An end-to-end system shall be developed for the collection, storage, contextualization and querying (through GUI/dashboards) of dark web threat actor intelligence-covering actor profiles, identifiers (handles, PGP keys, wallets etc.), hidden service infrastructure indicators, persona linkages, attribution confidence, category, last scan date and source. The system shall also provide the facility to export the result set in CSV, JSON and report formats.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, autonomous applied to a blockchain & cybersecurity problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Blockchain & Cybersecurity. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on infrastructure. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 17/30 -> Yellow verdict.

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an investigative system that gathers footprints of dark web threat actors across marketplaces and forums, spots technical misconfigurations that leak their real-world server location, and links their online activity to real-world identifying information for law enforcement attribution.
overview.why_it_matters: Dark web anonymity currently shields serious criminal activity, drug and arms sales, hacking services, money laundering, terror financing, from investigation. Genuine, technically sound de-anonymization capability directly supports law enforcement attribution in these cases.
pain_points: Tor hidden services make attribution of threat actors genuinely difficult for investigations.
Misconfigurations that could reveal origin servers require systematic, continuous monitoring to find.
Linking dark web activity to real-world identity requires correlating many disparate data sources.
overview.background: Dark web threat actors use Tor hidden services to conduct illegal activity while evading attribution, and current investigation methods for correlating misconfigurations, infrastructure clues, and identifying information aren't systematized.
overview.whats_being_asked: A system continuously gathering threat-actor footprints from dark web sources, finding Tor hidden-service misconfigurations linking to clearnet infrastructure, and mapping threat actors to real-world identifying information.
expected_solution: Continuous footprint collection from marketplaces, forums, deep web sources.
Tor hidden-service misconfiguration detection (exposed status pages, SSL cert reuse, banner leaks).
Clearnet infrastructure correlation from detected misconfigurations.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Systematic Tor misconfiguration detection combined with cross-source identity correlation is genuine, active cyber-threat-intelligence research territory, real technical and investigative sophistication.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires real OSINT collection infrastructure, Tor/network security understanding, and entity-resolution/correlation logic together, substantial technical breadth.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine cyber-threat-intelligence and OSINT expertise, a specialized, narrow field appropriate for a legitimate law-enforcement/national-security context.

innovation.note: Systematic misconfiguration detection plus cross-source identity correlation is genuine, sophisticated cyber-threat-intelligence work.

invention.note: Requires real OSINT infrastructure, Tor network understanding, and entity-resolution logic together.

technical_feasibility.tag: Tight for Real Dark Web Data Collection, Comfortable for a Simulated Demonstration
technical_feasibility.note: Real, ongoing dark web monitoring at hackathon scale is genuinely difficult and has real safety/legal considerations for a hackathon environment; a simulated or documented-methodology demonstration is the practical path.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly supports legitimate national-security and law-enforcement investigative capability.

architecture.note: Collection, misconfiguration-detection, and correlation modules together, genuine integration complexity.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with genuine cybersecurity/OSINT background, but real live dark web monitoring/interaction during a hackathon raises real practical and safety considerations. Scope your demonstration to the misconfiguration-detection methodology (which can be demonstrated against your own controlled test Tor hidden service) and a simulated correlation pipeline, rather than actually crawling live dark web marketplaces.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-specified, real technical methodology (specific misconfiguration types named: exposed status pages, SSL cert reuse, banner leaks) gives concrete, demonstrable technical targets.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Actually crawling live dark web marketplaces during a hackathon raises genuine practical and safety considerations, a controlled, self-hosted test environment is a much safer and still technically valid demonstration approach.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Set up your own controlled test Tor hidden service with deliberately introduced misconfigurations, and demonstrate your detection methodology against your own controlled infrastructure rather than actually crawling live dark web sources during the hackathon.

idea_0_4: Set up your own controlled test Tor hidden service with deliberately introduced misconfigurations (exposed status page, reused SSL cert) as a safe test environment.
Design your correlation methodology connecting detected misconfigurations to clearnet infrastructure.
Split: one person on misconfiguration-detection tooling, one on the correlation/entity-linking logic.
prototype_4_22: Build your misconfiguration-detection tooling and test it against your own controlled test hidden service.
Build your clearnet-correlation logic (matching detected server signatures to clearnet infrastructure).
Start entity-linking logic for connecting technical findings to identifying information.
integration_22_30: Connect detection and correlation into one coherent workflow, tested against your controlled environment.
Build the reporting output showing the investigative trail from detected misconfiguration to correlated infrastructure.
Test with multiple types of deliberately introduced misconfigurations to show detection breadth.
polish_30_36: Polish the reporting output for genuine investigator usability.
Rehearse a live demo against your own controlled test environment, showing the full detection-to-correlation pipeline.
Prepare to explain why you used a controlled test environment rather than live dark web crawling, and what real deployment would involve.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Demonstrate your misconfiguration-detection methodology live against your own controlled test Tor hidden service with a real introduced misconfiguration, and show the correlation pipeline tracing it to the correct clearnet infrastructure, that concrete, safe, working demonstration is stronger evidence than claims about live dark web crawling capability.

strengths: Very well-specified, real technical methodology with concrete, demonstrable targets.
weaknesses: Real live dark web interaction raises genuine safety/practicality concerns for a hackathon setting.
Full real-world identity correlation needs data sources beyond what's accessible in a hackathon.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced, with genuine cybersecurity domain knowledge for safe, realistic methodology demonstration.
team_fit.approach: Set up a controlled test environment first, this is both safer and gives you something concrete and real to demonstrate against.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Real understanding of Tor infrastructure and misconfiguration patterns, and careful, responsible scoping of what to actually test against (your own controlled environment, not live targets).
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: AI-scaffolded tooling pointed at live, real dark web targets during a hackathon without careful consideration raises genuine safety and legal concerns, a controlled test environment is the responsible approach.

data_resource_availability.status: No real dark web target data should be used for hackathon testing; a self-controlled test Tor hidden service is the appropriate, safe demonstration environment.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, controlled test environment construction is the intended, responsible approach here.

judge_qna.question: Did you actually crawl or interact with live dark web marketplaces during this hackathon?
judge_qna.strong_answer: No, and explain why directly, we built and tested our detection methodology against our own controlled Tor hidden service with deliberately introduced misconfigurations, this is both safer and still technically demonstrates the real detection capability.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would real deployment against live dark web sources require in terms of legal authorization and operational security?

judge_qna.question: How does your misconfiguration detection actually work technically?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific detection methodology against your controlled test environment, showing the introduced misconfiguration and how your tooling correctly identified and correlated it.
judge_qna.follow_up: What other misconfiguration types beyond what you tested would a comprehensive system need to detect?
